disclaimer: Every target below is an illustrative starting point adapted from adjacent domains (reliability engineering, DORA release metrics, software-quality defect KPIs, HIL test automation, model-coverage practice). None is confirmed Alpine practice. Targets are to be baselined and agreed with the Head of CSG before they mean anything.

categories.name: Simulator Reliability & Availability
categories.intent: Booked DIL time is scarce and expensive. This category answers: when the simulator was booked, did the control systems work?

categories.name: SECU Release Quality & Cadence
categories.intent: A failed release on session day burns irreplaceable driver time. Throughput and stability are read together, never one traded for the other.

categories.name: Fault Diagnosis & Turnaround
categories.intent: How fast faults are handled under session pressure, and whether they stay fixed.

categories.name: System Familiarity & Model Fidelity
categories.intent: Correlation is the point of the simulator. This category tracks whether the DIL mirrors the car.

categories.name: Documentation & Knowledge Bridging
categories.intent: The institutional memory that de-risks the team's bus factor — a named deliverable of the role.

categories.name: Communication & Stakeholder Satisfaction
categories.intent: Much of the role's value is judged by the people it supports. A structured survey turns that into a trackable signal.

categories.name: Technical Development & Tooling
categories.intent: The 'make things better' half of the role, plus the wider CSG work that otherwise goes invisible at review.

kpis.name: DIL Control-System Availability
kpis.what: Share of scheduled simulator time in which chassis control systems were fully operational.
kpis.why: Booked DIL time is a scarce, high-value resource; lost time costs car-development throughput directly.
kpis.method: Per-session log of scheduled vs productive minutes, with a disruption cause on every loss.
kpis.formula: Σ productive minutes ÷ Σ scheduled minutes × 100
kpis.cadence: Logged per session, rolled up monthly and quarterly.
kpis.note: Cultural anchor, not a target: the F1 Standard ECU's public field record is zero reported in-race failures since 2008 (manufacturer statement, McLaren Applied).

kpis.name: Control-Attributable Session Loss
kpis.what: Sessions delayed, shortened or scrapped by a control-system or SECU issue — as distinct from motion platform, models or IT.
kpis.why: Isolates the share of downtime this role actually owns, so availability is not read as a personal score for someone else's outage.
kpis.method: Count of control-attributable disruptions, with every loss root-caused into a category.
kpis.formula: count(sessions where disruption cause = control system)
kpis.cadence: Per session; reviewed monthly, targeted quarterly.

kpis.name: Control-Fault MTBF / MTTR
kpis.what: Mean operating hours between control-system faults, and mean time to restore during a session.
kpis.why: MTBF shows the system getting more robust; MTTR shows responsiveness under pressure. Availability alone hides which one moved.
kpis.method: Operational hours and fault counts from the session log; restore time captured per fault.
kpis.formula: MTBF = operational hours ÷ fault count · MTTR = Σ restore minutes ÷ fault count

kpis.name: Release First-Time-Pass Rate
kpis.what: Share of SECU release packages that deploy and run correctly on session day with no hotfix and no rollback.
kpis.why: The direct analogue of the DORA change-failure rate. Elite performers sit near a 5% change-failure rate; here the cost of failure is driver time that cannot be bought back.
kpis.method: Release register: one row per package, flagged for session-day intervention or rollback.
kpis.formula: releases with no session-day intervention ÷ total releases × 100

kpis.name: Escaped-Defect Rate & Detection Efficiency
kpis.what: Defects found live in session that pre-event HIL and bench testing should have caught, expressed as detection efficiency.
kpis.why: The truest measure of pre-release test effectiveness. Mature teams sustain 85–95% detection efficiency; the severity split matters more than the headline number.
kpis.method: Every defect tagged found-before or found-after release, with severity.
kpis.formula: defects found pre-release ÷ (pre-release + escaped) × 100
tools: Defect tracker with severity + fix-version fields
kpis.note: Read as a process signal, never as blame. An escape should start a test-coverage conversation, not a search for who let it through.

kpis.name: Release Lead Time & Readiness Buffer
kpis.what: Share of packages validated and staged at least one working day before session day, plus the median lead time from spec freeze to validated package.
kpis.why: A healthy buffer is what removes session-day risk. Lead time is the throughput half of the pair — a fast release that lands at 6am on session day is not a good release.
kpis.method: Timestamps from ticket or spec-freeze to validated-package Git tag; buffer measured against the event date.
kpis.formula: releases with buffer ≥ 24h ÷ total releases × 100

kpis.name: HIL Regression Pass Rate & Automated Coverage
kpis.what: Share of automated HIL regression cases passing on each release candidate, and the share of SECU functions covered by at least one automated case.
kpis.why: Automated regression is what stops a small fix creating a new control problem somewhere else. Coverage growth is the leading indicator; pass rate is the gate.
kpis.method: dSPACE AutomationDesk pass/fail logs parsed per release; coverage from the function register.
kpis.formula: cases passed ÷ cases run × 100 · coverage = functions with ≥1 automated case ÷ total functions × 100

kpis.name: In-Session Fault Resolution Time
kpis.what: Median time from fault raised to workaround or fix while the session is live.
kpis.why: The pressurised-environment competency the role is hired for. Median plus the long tail says more than an average.
kpis.method: Session log timestamps, segmented by fault class so the playbook can target the worst class.
kpis.formula: median(resolved_at − raised_at) over in-session faults

kpis.name: Root-Cause Closure Rate
kpis.what: Share of faults with a documented root cause and corrective action closed within the agreed SLA.
kpis.why: Speed of the workaround is not the same as quality of the fix. This is what stops the same fault reappearing next event.
kpis.method: Ticket system with a mandatory root-cause field and an SLA clock.
kpis.formula: faults root-caused within SLA ÷ resolved faults × 100

kpis.name: Fault Recurrence Rate
kpis.what: Share of faults that reappear after being marked resolved.
kpis.why: Tests the durability of the fix rather than the speed of it — the counterweight that keeps resolution time honest.
kpis.method: Linked or duplicate tickets against the original fault ID.
kpis.formula: recurring faults ÷ resolved faults × 100

kpis.name: DIL-vs-Car Configuration Alignment
kpis.what: Share of tracked control-system parameters where the DIL SECU matches the current car standard, or carries a documented and justified difference.
kpis.why: Correlation is the whole point of the simulator. An undocumented difference is worse than a known one — it silently degrades every conclusion drawn from the session.
kpis.method: Automated diff of DIL vs car configuration exports; a difference counts as aligned only if it is deliberately documented.
kpis.formula: (matched items + documented differences) ÷ tracked items × 100

kpis.name: Baseline Currency
kpis.what: Lag between a car-side SECU software or calibration change and the corresponding DIL baseline update.
kpis.why: Stale baselines degrade correlation quietly — nothing fails, the answers are just wrong.
kpis.method: Date of car release compared with date DIL baseline updated, per release.
kpis.formula: median(DIL baseline date − car release date)

kpis.name: Model & Requirements Test Coverage
kpis.what: Decision, condition, MC/DC and signal-range coverage of the control models in this remit.
kpis.why: Coverage gaps surface missing requirements and unintended functionality — the cheapest place to find a defect is before it reaches the rig.
kpis.method: Simulink Coverage cumulative reports, aggregated across models under remit.
kpis.formula: mean of decision, condition, MC/DC and signal-range coverage

kpis.name: DIL-vs-Car Difference Catalogue Completeness
kpis.what: Share of known configuration and usage differences captured in one maintained catalogue.
kpis.why: A named deliverable of the role, and the institutional memory that stops the team depending on one person's head.
kpis.method: Documented differences over differences identified in periodic audits.
kpis.formula: documented differences ÷ identified differences × 100

kpis.name: Documentation Freshness
kpis.what: Share of catalogue and procedure pages reviewed or updated within the agreed window.
kpis.why: Documentation only earns trust if it is current. A stale page is consulted once and then never again.
kpis.method: Platform last-reviewed timestamps, 90-day window.
kpis.formula: pages reviewed within window ÷ total pages × 100

kpis.name: Procedure / SOP Coverage
kpis.what: Recurring simulator procedures with a signed-off SOP, against the total identified.
kpis.why: Reduces setup error and removes the operator dependence on one engineer being in the room.
kpis.method: SOP register reviewed against the procedure inventory.
kpis.formula: signed-off SOPs ÷ identified procedures × 100

kpis.name: Stakeholder Satisfaction (360-style)
kpis.what: Short periodic rating from drivers, race engineers, vehicle performance and the Simulator Section Leader on clarity of guidance, responsiveness and confidence in the rig.
kpis.why: Much of this role's value is judged subjectively by the people it supports. A structured survey turns corridor opinion into a trackable signal.
kpis.method: Anonymous 3–5 question survey per group, aggregated as the mean of group means so no group dominates.
kpis.formula: mean over rater groups of (group mean rating)
kpis.cadence: Quarterly, or per major event block.
kpis.note: Anonymity floor: a group returning fewer than 3 raters is merged with an adjacent group before reporting, never published alone.

kpis.name: Simulator Fidelity Confidence
kpis.what: Driver and engineer confidence that simulator control-system behaviour matches the car, corroborated with an objective sim-vs-track delta where data allow.
kpis.why: Fidelity confidence is what makes simulator time actionable for setup decisions. Subjective and objective must be read together — either alone misleads.
kpis.method: Survey item paired with an ATLAS-derived delta on selected channels.
kpis.formula: mean(fidelity item) · objective delta = mean |sim − track| on tracked channels

kpis.name: Debrief Contribution & Turnaround
kpis.what: Timeliness and usefulness of post-session control-system input into the standard debrief.
kpis.why: The simulator's value is realised in the debrief loop. Input that arrives after the decision has been made counts for nothing.
kpis.method: Structured post-session debrief template with a due time and a usefulness rating from the receiving engineer.
kpis.formula: debriefs submitted on time ÷ sessions × 100

kpis.name: Development Delivery Rate
kpis.what: Improvements, tools and HIL capabilities delivered against a jointly agreed quarterly roadmap.
kpis.why: Keeps the development half of the role visible and prioritised rather than squeezed out by session support.
kpis.method: OKR-style: 2–3 focus items per quarter, committed with the manager at the start of the cycle.
kpis.formula: roadmap items delivered ÷ items committed × 100

kpis.name: Operator-Effort / Setup-Time Reduction
kpis.what: Measured reduction in manual setup time and configuration-error rate from tooling built in this role.
kpis.why: Turns 'I built a tool' into 'the rig gains X minutes every session' — the form of the claim that survives a review conversation.
kpis.method: Before/after setup timing on the same procedure, plus configuration-error counts.
kpis.formula: (setup minutes before − after) ÷ before × 100

kpis.name: CSG Cross-Task Contribution
kpis.what: Support delivered to the wider Controls & Systems Group on rigs, dynos, tests and car tasks.
kpis.why: The role explicitly includes non-simulator CSG work. Logging it stops that contribution being invisible at review time.
kpis.method: A simple log of cross-group tasks and their outcomes — count is the prompt, the outcomes are the substance.
kpis.formula: count(cross-group tasks in quarter)
kpis.note: Deliberately a weak quantitative signal. Read the outcome notes, not the count.
